card.name: Plural S on PATIENT in all caps
card.fires_on: The final S of PATIENTS or INDIVIDUALS in all-capital warning text, and the word SHOULD right after a singular patient or condition. It is most common before phrases like WITH IMPAIRED RENAL FUNCTION.

modes.label: Plural ending on patient
modes.description: The S that completes PATIENTS or INDIVIDUALS in capitalized label headings and warnings.
modes.example: DOSAGE GUIDELINES FOR PATIENT<<S>> WITH IMPAIRED RENAL FUNCTION

modes.label: SHOULD after the subject
modes.description: The word SHOULD directly after a capitalized patient or condition subject.
modes.example: ORDINARILY, A PATIENT<< SHOULD>> NOT BE PLACED ON AND/OR

card.writes: It promotes word endings such as 'S, ERS, ER and ING, which fits adding a suffix to the current word.
card.plain: It marks the plural S at the end of PATIENTS in capitalized label warnings, usually before a kidney or liver function phrase.
